# MDL Pre-flight Checklist — STOP conditions before writing any script
**Applies to:** any mxcli project.
**Purpose:** Before drafting any MDL script, check every planned operation against this table. Each STOP row was born from a real MPR corruption or silent runtime failure — not theoretical concerns. Skipping this check has caused project-unloadable corruption every time.

**Source:** Generalized from a live Mendix 11.12.0 Beta project, 2026-07-06/07. Incident detail stays in that project's own `bug-logs/` — only the generalizable rule is here.

**Version context:** a retired row keeps its number (other skills cite `STOP #n`). Why each went, the version notes and every row's full root cause: `process/baseline-incident-history.md` § PF1. If in doubt about a rule, retest on your version and stamp the result in `bug-logs/mxcli-bugs.md`.

**Still a STOP:** workflow `DECISION` activities (BUG-76) — `learned-workflow-patterns.md` §8 Warning 1; never force one with `--no-check`. Before a first `marketplace install`, read the #879 entry in `bug-logs/mxcli-bugs.md`.


> Source: `skills/learned-mdl-preflight.md` § Step 0 — choose the write mode
## Step 0 — choose the write mode (do this first, before the STOP table)

**Default: the mxcli CLI, through `./bin/exec.sh script.mdl`** (Studio Pro closed). On mxcli v0.24.0 it writes everything MDL can express — domain model, microflows (inline association sets included), pages (combobox and `DropdownFilter` in association mode, cross-module association datasources), access rules, security level and project settings, navigation, workflows, marketplace installs. `exec.sh` snapshots first, runs the mxbuild gate after, and restores on failure. Run `mxcli check <script> -p <app>.mpr --references` before it — `exec` refuses less than `check` flags (last gotcha below).

**Studio Pro by hand — only for what MDL cannot express**, e.g. the DataGrid2 customContent conditionals in row 1 and the items in `learned-mdl-cannot-express.md`. Save and close Studio Pro before the next CLI write, and snapshot first; a CLI write under an open Studio Pro with unsaved changes is a split-brain.

**Not MDL at all.** Sometimes no mode can express the change, e.g. an association owner change, and the answer is a script that edits the `.mpr` directly. Run it as `./bin/exec.sh --patch <script> [args]`, never bare. The script gets the model path as its first argument. It gets the same snapshot, mxbuild gate, restore and BUILD-LOG row as MDL, and it is kept only on a verified gate. The header of `project-bin/exec.sh` has the details. Build the script on `bin/mxpatch.py` (find unit/element, set with an expected old value, write the unit and its ContentsHash together): a unit written without its hash is restored by the run's `mxcli fix hashes` check (mxbuild cannot see a stale hash). Owner **both** and the association type can be changed in MDL (0 errors, v0.24.0). Flipping FROM/TO with `create or modify association` prints "Modified association" but `describe` still shows the old direction — a silent no-op, so read it back.

**Also decide, per document, where it lands.** Any operation that *creates* a document — page, snippet, microflow, nanoflow — needs its folder chosen now and written into the `folder` property of the same statement, not fixed afterwards. Read the path off the brief's `### Document folder plan`; when there is no row for it, derive it per `module-folder-convention.md` ("Deciding the path"), and escalate rather than guess when the feature group is unclear. Omitting `folder` is legal MDL that silently drops the document at module root — no error, no gate, and a cleanup job later that nobody schedules.

**Companion skills:** `bug-logs/mxcli-bugs.md` (bug detail), `iterative-build-loop.md` (exec discipline), `learned-microflow-patterns.md` (annotation and association rules)

## The checklist — run before writing a single line of MDL

🔎 = `bin/mdl-scan.sh` flags it in `exec.sh`.

Each row keeps one failure clause; the full root cause is in `process/baseline-incident-history.md` § PF1. `Kind` names what the script writes — rows of kind `any` apply to every script.

| # | If your script will… | Then… | Fails as | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | `DROP` + `CREATE`, `create or modify` or `create or replace` any document **another script also edits** — an aggregator microflow, an after-startup chain, a navigation profile | **STOP → `describe` the live document first, diff your restatement against that dump, and name in the script header which call sites you preserved. A new owner adds `-- supersedes: <script>`; drafting ahead of unrun scripts, `bin/describe-baseline.sh stamp <script>` after the DESCRIBE (exec.sh only warns).** Prefer an in-place edit where your mxcli has one: `alter navigation` / `alter menu` (v0.28+, mendixlabs/mxcli#1522), and `alter microflow` inside loop bodies or `replace body of` (v0.29+, ako/mxcli#1693). Whole-document restatement makes losing a sibling script's edit the *default* outcome, not an unlikely one. | A sibling script's call silently vanished; `mx check` 0 errors, lint's orphan rule exempts `ACT_` (2026-08-26). | any |
| 22 | Write a script containing ANY non-idempotent statement — `alter entity … add attribute`, bare `CREATE ASSOCIATION`, bare `CREATE MICROFLOW`/`CREATE PAGE` on a name that may already exist | **STOP → use the `create or modify` form for every statement, and give every document exactly ONE owning script.** From mxcli v0.27 any write failure **rolls back the whole run**, so one non-idempotent statement, even last, fails every re-run. The property to hold is that `mdlsource/` replays cleanly against an EMPTY app; that is one command and it is the only thing that proves it. | v0.27+: nothing written; older: earlier statements stay written. `mx check` 0 errors — the exit code is the only signal: never ignore it. | any |
| 23 | Name any document or entity that **might already exist** — `create or modify` on an entity, or any `create or replace` on a page, layout or microflow | **STOP → run `mxcli diff -p <app>.mpr <script>.mdl --format struct` FIRST.** It is read-only, it takes a second, and it prints exactly what the script would add and what it would REMOVE. (`exec` itself only warns — v0.24.0: `create or modify entity Mod.Order drops 6 existing member(s)` — and then writes.) Read the `-` lines before you exec, every time. Rules 21 and 22 tell you to write `create or modify` and to give each document one owner; this is the check that the name you chose is actually free. | `create or modify` on an entity **replaces** its attribute set; `mx check` stays clean. `diff` also prints false `- Attribute` lines (BUG-146): check each against `DESCRIBE ENTITY`. | any |
| 1c 2 3 5 6 6b 7 8 9 10 11 13 15 17 27 | *(retired 2026-09-30 — numbers kept for `STOP #n` citations; why each went: `process/baseline-incident-history.md` § PF1)* | | | |

**Default to the CLI for everything in the table above that is not a STOP row** (`./bin/exec.sh`, Studio Pro closed).


> Source: `skills/learned-mdl-preflight.md` § MDL gotchas
## MDL gotchas (quick reference — common traps)

None of these needs a STOP, but each passes `mxcli check` and fails later — at native `mx check`, on SP open, or silently at runtime. The generated project `CLAUDE.md` already covers `EXTENDS` placement and the missing `CASE`/`TRY` statements; [[learned-microflow-patterns]] covers `toString()` on enums. Only what lives nowhere else is kept here.

- **Quote / unquote retry rule:** when any identifier fails at `mxcli check`, `mx check`, or runtime, try the other form before concluding anything. Applies to every identifier position. One form always works; the other may parse and still write wrong BSON.
- **Enumeration values named with reserved words** (`Receive`, `Move`, `Count`, `Open`, …) cannot be targeted by `alter enumeration … modify value` — v0.24.0 gives a parse error (`mismatched input 'Receive' expecting IDENTIFIER`), quoted or not, before any write. Use `create or modify enumeration` — which **replaces** the enum, so restate the full value set and the doc comment. Change captions only; renaming a value NAME silently breaks every reference and `mxcli check` will not say so.
- **Grants are co-located with the element, never deferred to one `security.mdl`:** `grant execute` ends the microflow script, `grant view` the page script, entity access the domain script — the entity and its access rule are one unit, same script, same commit. mxbuild raises no error for a missing grant; the only symptom is a blank screen or CE2729 once a non-admin role opens the page. A `roles.mdl` that only *creates* roles is fine. Pre-flight per entity: access rule in the same script? every module role that needs it granted? every module role composed into a user role? non-persistent DTOs — read/write only (CONV006)?
- **`mxcli check` does not catch corruption.** Every STOP row above is grammatically valid MDL that `check` passes; only mxbuild or SP open reveals the damage. Run the real mxbuild gate after every exec (`iterative-build-loop.md`).
- **mxcli v0.25 — keep the skills' spellings, never add `mdl 1;`.** The spellings in these skills (`count($L)`, `on error { … }`, `show page M.P($Obj = $Obj)`, `create or replace`) parse on v0.24.0 *and* v0.25.0; v0.25 only warns (`MDL-DEPR*`, "refused from `mdl 2`"). The new spellings (`count $L`, `on error begin … end error`, `P(Obj = $Obj)`) fail `check` on v0.24 — don't "modernise" a script the team may still run there. The hazard is the dialect header: v0.24 rejects it (`line 1:4 extraneous input '1'`), and under it v0.25 changes meanings — `show entity M.E` becomes an error (use `describe entity` / `list entities`; `-c` and the REPL already read this way), and `retrieve … limit 1` returns a *list* (use `first`) while `check` still passes. So strip the `mdl 1;` line from `describe` output before pasting it into a script, and never mix dialects in one file. Moving a whole file to mdl 1 on purpose: `mxcli fmt --upgrade -w -p <app>.mpr <script>`, then `check -p --references`, then exec twice (the second writes nothing).
- **`exec` is not `check`.** v0.24.0: `exec` refuses on reference errors and a few hard checks (MDL043, MDL044, MDL070, MDL-WIDGET14/19/24) but still writes scripts that plain `mxcli check` flags — e.g. an enum concatenation (E004). Run `mxcli check <script> -p <app>.mpr --references` yourself and read every error and warning before `exec`; a clean `exec` is not a clean `check`.

> Source: `skills/learned-mdl-preflight.md` § Final self-check
## Final self-check (mandatory before reporting back)

After drafting a script, re-read it line by line against the table above — not just the mental pre-check you did before writing. Conditional visibility inside datagrid customContent columns, quoted DataGrid 2 association paths, unprefixed association steps in expressions and a quoted `Editable:` can creep in during drafting without intent. `mxcli check --references` will not catch them. This re-read is the actual corruption-prevention step.

**Then diff it before you exec it** (rule 23): `mxcli diff -p <app>.mpr <script>.mdl --format struct` is read-only and prints what the script would add *and remove*. The re-read above catches what you wrote; the diff catches what you did not know was already there — a name you believed free, an entity whose attribute set your `create or modify` would replace rather than extend. Read every `-` line.

**And check the size before you execute:** could you diagnose a failure of this script from the
error output alone, or would you be re-reading the whole file to find which unit broke? If the
latter, split it and say so in chat before executing — even when the build plan handed it to
you whole. A per-layer plan does not mean a layer is one script; see
`brd-to-build-plan.md` Step 3. Observed failure: a plan that put 13 microflows in one exec.

Isolate anything the other units depend on, group the rest by "would one failure explain the
others?", and do not over-split — every extra script is another approval prompt, and approval
fatigue hollows out RULE 1 as surely as an opaque mega-script does.

> Source: `skills/learned-microflow-patterns.md` § Association Direction — Reading SHOW ASSOCIATIONS Correctly
## Association Direction — Reading SHOW ASSOCIATIONS Correctly

Mendix association terminology is **opposite** to most ORMs:

| Mendix term | Mendix meaning | ORM meaning |
|-------------|---------------|-------------|
| Parent | MANY side — owns the FK column | ONE side |
| Child | ONE side — referenced entity | MANY side |

```
SHOW ASSOCIATIONS: Parent=ChoiceOrg, Child=OrderApplicationHeader
→ Many ChoiceOrg → One OrderApplicationHeader. ChoiceOrg has the FK.

DESCRIBE ASSOCIATION: from ChoiceOrg to OrderApplicationHeader
→ from = MANY (owner), to = ONE (referenced)

Studio Pro visual (ground truth): ChoiceOrg (*) ──► (1) OrderApplicationHeader
```

**Never propose flipping an association based solely on SHOW ASSOCIATIONS output** — the Parent/Child labels are misleading. Verify from the Studio Pro visual (`*` = many, `1` = one) before any association change.

# Security Is Not a Later Script

**Applies to:** any Mendix module built through mxcli/MDL where security is scripted
separately from the domain model.
**Purpose:** stop the "perfect page nobody can read" failure: entity access, role mapping, ready-checks.

Written after a module build shipped a structurally perfect page that no user could read; a user
found it in a Studio Pro error list, not the pipeline.

**Companion:** `tool-output-is-not-ground-truth.md`.

---

## What happened

Three security omissions, all found at the end:

| # | Omission | Surfaced as |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No entity access rules on any module entity | 12 × `CE2729 No read access to attribute 'X'` |
| 2 | Module role never mapped into a *user* role | silent — page invisible to non-admins |
| 3 | The source system's own roles never modelled | not surfaced at all; still open at handoff |

## The reasoning error worth remembering

The build script asserted: "Non-persistent entities carry no row-level security, so there are no
entity access rules to grant."

**This is wrong.** It conflates two things:

| | Non-persistent entities |
|---|---|
| **Row-level** security (XPath constraints) | genuinely absent — there are no rows to constrain |
| **Member-level** access (read/write per attribute) | **required** — without it no widget can bind |

A page bound to a non-persistent entity with no access rules renders and displays nothing.

**A wrong justification is more dangerous than no justification:** an unexplained gap invites
review; a confident one closes the question.

## The invisible one

Omission 2 produced no error at all. `grant view on page X to Module.User` succeeds, and the
security matrix looks populated. But if no *user role* contains `Module.User`, nobody holds it.

It was masked because **mxcli auto-adds the new module role to `Administrator`**: testing as
admin worked, a demo user saw an empty menu.

```bash
# the check that catches it
./mxcli -p app.mpr -c "DESCRIBE USER ROLE 'User'" | grep -o "YourModule\.[A-Za-z]*"
```

If every sibling module appears in that role and yours doesn't, that is the bug.

---

## THE RULE: entities and their access rules are one unit

Write `grant ... on Entity` in the **same script** as `create entity`. Not a later "security
script", not a "grants pass".

Splitting them leaves a model that is complete and unusable, and nothing compares the two.

## THE SECOND RULE: a ready-check must mean *built*, not *decided*

A module brief had a full security section and a ready-check reading **"Security model confirmed"**.
It was confirmed as *designed*, not *built*; no gate compared brief and model.

Any ready-check item about the model must be verified against the model:

```bash
./mxcli -p app.mpr -c "SHOW SECURITY MATRIX IN <Module>"
```

An empty `## Entity Access` section on a module that has pages means security is **not
done**, whatever the brief says.

---

## CE2729 also fires from navigation and page microflows

Field run (mxcli v0.26.0): eight failed gates, grants written for the page's own role only.

| Cause | Write it so |
|---|---|
| `home page Module.Page` on the **default** profile, for a role with no access to that page | Keep the default home page one **every role can view**; add `home page Module.Page for <UserRole>;` per role that needs its own |
| A page data-source microflow granted `execute` only to the designing role | `grant execute on microflow M.DS_X to` **every module role that can reach the page**, in the microflow's script |
| Re-running a partial `create or modify navigation` resets the menu | Give the **final** profile its own last script; never re-run an earlier one |

## Pre-flight checklist — before calling any module complete

1. `SHOW SECURITY MATRIX IN <Module>` — is `Entity Access` populated?
2. `DESCRIBE USER ROLE '<role>'` — does a real user role contain the module role?
3. Do the entity grants cover **create** where a microflow or import mapping constructs
   objects (non-persistent DTOs: everything a mapping populates)?
4. Do editable widgets have **write** on their bound attributes, not just read?
5. Does every role that can reach a page have page access **and** execute on each microflow it calls? (CE2729 above)
6. Does the built model match the module brief's security table — and if not deliberately,
   is the deviation written down?

## On `create`/`delete` and lint rule CONV006

CONV006 discourages granting create/delete in access rules. It targets **persistent**
entities holding real data. Non-persistent DTOs populated by an import mapping require
`create` on every entity the mapping instantiates; restricting it breaks the mapping and
protects nothing, as the upstream system revalidates every call.

Note the deviation explicitly rather than tripping the rule silently.

# Detection gaps — what each verification rung is blind to

**Applies to:** any mxcli project
**Purpose:** the register of MDL constructs that pass one or more verification rungs and still
fail later, with the **first oracle that catches each**. Use it before trusting a green result
and when a runtime symptom appears over a green model.

Every row was found in the field: **a green result only certifies what its rung can see.**

**Hit or worked around a tool bug?** Append a row now: `bin/file-bugs.sh --add --target mxcli|toolkit --title T --repro R --expected E --actual A` (`docs/bugs.jsonl`, local id `PBUG-NN`); the same script later redacts it; only a human files it (`!bin/file-bugs.sh --file PBUG-NN`, denied to agents).


> Source: `skills/learned-detection-gaps.md` § The ladder
## The ladder

1. `mxcli check --references` — MDL grammar and reference syntax. Catches the least.
2. `mxcli exec` "success" — the write completed; says nothing about what was written.
3. `DESCRIBE ...` read-back — mxcli's own lenient reader; it normalises and omits what it cannot represent, so it can hide corruption.
4. Native `mx check` / mxbuild — the real model loader. Catches structural and expression
   errors; blind to runtime wiring.
5. Studio Pro's own GUI loader — catches BSON-structural corruption `mx check` sometimes
   passes (see `scriptable-sp-verification.md`).
6. **Live runtime observation** — a browser retrieve, `/xas/` traffic, a DB row count. The
   only rung that verifies *behaviour*. **Only as true as the harness that reads it** (operating rule 3).

> Source: `skills/learned-detection-gaps.md` § Operating rules that fall out of this table
## Operating rules that fall out of this table

1. **A green rung certifies only what that rung reads.** "Passes check and exec" is a claim
   about syntax and about a write completing — never about what was stored, and never about
   runtime behaviour.
2. **Read-back is not ground truth either.** `DESCRIBE` hides three rows of this table; it is a
   lenient reader, not an oracle (`skills/tool-output-is-not-ground-truth.md`).
3. **Rung 6 has its own gaps: the instrument can lie.** A screenshot is evidence only while the
   harness is correct: one that resizes a loaded page instead of creating one context per width
   produced seven false "drawer covers content" defects (`ui-loop.md` → "The screenshot harness
   is an instrument too"). The tell is uniformity: a defect on every screen at exactly one width
   is the camera.
4. **For anything that wires behaviour** (calculated attributes, import mappings, filters,
   datasources), the acceptance test is a **live observation**: a runtime retrieve, the
   `/xas/` payload, a row count — not any static check. `testing-shape.md`'s false-green
   register is the verification-side companion of this authoring-side table.
5. **Add a row when the family grows.** The entry condition is exactly: "passed rung N,
   failed at rung >N, confirmed in the field." File the bug in `bug-logs/mxcli-bugs.md`
   first; this table carries the one-line lesson and the pointer.

# Retesting a learned rule before you obey it

**Applies to:** any mxcli project.

**Purpose:** a `learned-*.md` rule is a measurement of a *binary at a moment*, not a law. mxcli
ships frequently; every STOP, workaround and "not supported" in this toolkit has a half-life.
This file is the cheap probe that decides whether a rule still holds, and the discipline for
writing one down so the next reader can re-run it instead of re-deriving it.

## When this fires

Before you act on a learned rule that would make your work **more complicated than the obvious
approach** — a STOP that routes you to Studio Pro or MCP, a "wrap it in a nanoflow", a "not
supported, use X instead". Rules that merely tell you the correct syntax cost nothing to obey;
rules that add a workaround cost a lot, and are the ones that rot expensively.

Do **not** fire on every rule on every session. The trigger is: *this rule is about to cost me
a detour, and it carries a version stamp older than my binary.*

## The probe, in order — stop at the first honest answer

1. **`./mxcli --version`.** Compare against the rule's stamp. Same or older binary → the rule
   stands, obey it. Newer → continue.
2. **`./mxcli check <scratch>.mdl`** on the smallest script that expresses the forbidden thing.
   A parse error is a real answer: the grammar is absent, stop here.
3. **Exec it and read a real gate.** `mxcli check` passing is not evidence — most of this
   toolkit's STOP rules describe constructs that pass `check` and corrupt on write. Run the
   project's `bin/exec.sh` (or exec + `mx check`/mxbuild) and read the **mxbuild verdict**, not
   the exit code. Then `DESCRIBE` the element and look at what was actually stored.
4. **Drop the probe.** A scratch element left in a real model is a defect you introduced while
   proving one did not exist.

## What a probe must never do

- Never conclude from **documentation**. `mxcli syntax` and the bundled `.ai-context/skills/`
  are not the grammar; the parser is. The incident that produced this file: a rule stating "MDL
  has no show-message activity anywhere" was derived by reading two skill files' statement
  lists. The activity had existed the whole time; `mxcli syntax` documents it nowhere, so the
  documentation sweep could only ever return "absent". Worse, mxcli's own bundled
  `write-nanoflows.md` used a **level-first grammar the shipped binary rejects** — so an agent
  that did find the skill got a parse error and reached the same wrong conclusion.
- Never conclude from a **binary's embedded strings or examples**. `strings ./mxcli` will happily
  show you syntax the shipped grammar refuses.
- Never conclude from **one green `mxcli check`**. See step 3.

## Writing the result down — four things, or it rots again

Whatever the verdict, edit the rule **in place** in its `learned-*.md`. A retest recorded
somewhere else is a second source of truth, and the older, louder one wins.

1. **Both stamps.** The binary and Mendix version you tested on, and the date. A rule with no
   stamp cannot be retested by anyone; it can only be believed or ignored.
2. **The verdict word, in the first sentence** — `STILL HOLDS`, `DOES NOT REPRODUCE`, or
   `RETIRED`. A reader skimming for the trigger must not have to reach paragraph three.
3. **The evidence, with its denominator** — what you ran, how many cases, and which gate said
   what ("a probe microflow with a bare literal, a concatenation and all three severity levels,
   executed, real mxbuild 0 errors"). "Retested, fine" is not a receipt.
4. **Keep the old rule underneath, marked as history.** Projects pin different binaries; a rule
   deleted outright strands every project still on the old one. Say which binary each half
   applies to.

## Completion criteria

The retest is done when: the rule's own text carries a verdict word and two version stamps; the
probe element is gone from the model (`SHOW MICROFLOWS`/`SHOW PAGES` returns 0 matches for its
name); and every *other* file in the toolkit asserting the same thing has been reconciled —
`grep -ril '<the claim>' skills/ bug-logs/` returning exactly the files you edited. That last
check is not optional: the show-message incident had the correct knowledge in
`learned-microflow-patterns.md` and the flatly wrong claim in `learned-popup-feedback-pattern.md`
**at the same time**, in the same repo, for three weeks. Two files, two answers, no one reading
both.

Rules for kinds any, entity: STOP rows 3/3 listed
